The '''2010–11 Football League Cup''' (known as the '''[[Carling]] Cup''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 51st season of the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]], a knock-out competition for the top 92 [[Association football|football]] clubs played in [[English football league system]].<ref name="key_dates">{{cite news|title=2010/11 Carling Cup Dates Revealed |url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/latestnews/20100308/key-dates-revealed_2245681_1987488 |publisher=The Football League |date=8 March 2010 |access-date=8 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100311043329/http://www.football-league.co.uk/latestnews/20100308/key-dates-revealed_2245681_1987488 |archive-date=11 March 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The winners were granted a place in the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]]. However, in cases where a team had already gained a place in European competition via their league position or progress in other cup competitions, their place in the Europa League was deferred to the next best-placed league side not already qualified for European competitions.

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] were the [[2010 Football League Cup final|defending champions]] for the second successive season, but were knocked out in the fifth round by [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].

The [[2011 Football League Cup final|final]] was contested on 27 February 2011 between [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]]. Birmingham were the surprise 2–1 winners in the final to win just the second [[major trophy]] in their history.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://theglobalherald.com/football-arsenal-1-2-birmingham-carling-cup-final-2011-result/12195/ |title=Football: Arsenal 1-2 Birmingham, Carling Cup final 2011 Result |work=The Global Herald|date=27 February 2011 |access-date=27 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717000540/http://theglobalherald.com/football-arsenal-1-2-birmingham-carling-cup-final-2011-result/12195/ |archive-date=17 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/birminghams-glory-leaves-arsenal-to-face-defining-run-2227471.html |title=Birmingham's glory leaves Arsenal to face defining run |date=27 February 2011 |work=The Independent |access-date=28 February 2011 |archive-date=3 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303010921/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/birminghams-glory-leaves-arsenal-to-face-defining-run-2227471.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Birmingham City also won their first major trophy since 1963 (also a [[1963 Football League Cup final|League Cup]]) and earned a place in European competition for the first time since 1961.

== First round ==
The draw for the first round took place on 16 June 2010, with matches played two months later on 10 August 2010.<ref name="key_dates"/><ref name="bbcdraw">{{cite news |title=Carling Cup 2010/11 – first round draw details |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/8742947.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 June 2010 |access-date=16 June 2010 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100617061611/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/8742947.stm| archive-date= 17 June 2010 <!--DASHBot-->| url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] received a First Round bye as the highest ranked teams from the previous season's league placings. The other 70 of the 72 [[2010–11 Football League|Football League]] clubs competed in the first round, divided into North and South sections. Each section was divided equally into a pot of seeded clubs and a pot of unseeded clubs. Clubs' rankings depend upon their finishing position in the [[2009–10 in English football|2009–10 season]].

== Second round ==
The 13 Premier League teams not involved in European competitions entered at this stage along with the winners from the first round plus Burnley and Hull City, who had received a First Round bye. If there is a draw at full-time there will be extra time followed by a penalty shootout if the scores are still level. From the second round onwards, the teams are no longer split geographically. The draw for the second round took place on the evening of 11 August 2010, after the first-round matches had been completed, and the matches were played in the week beginning 23 August 2010.<ref name="key_dates"/>

== Third round ==
The seven [[2010–11 Premier League|Premier League]] teams involved in European competition entered at this stage, along with the winners from the second round. The draw for the Third Round took place on 28 August 2010, after the second-round games had been played. The matches were played in the week beginning 20 September 2010.<ref name="key_dates"/> [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] were the only [[2010–11 Football League Two|League Two]] side to reach this round of the tournament.

== Fourth round ==
The Fourth Round draw took place on 25 September 2010, and the matches were played on the week commencing 25 October 2010.<ref name="key_dates"/> For the second consecutive round, [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] was the lowest ranked remaining side, being the lone representative from [[2010–11 Football League Two|League Two]]. All four leagues involved in this competition had representation in the Fourth Round for the first time since the [[2006–07 Football League Cup|2006–07 competition]].

== Fifth round ==
[[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] was the lowest ranked side left in the competition, and the sole remaining representative of the [[2010–11 Football League Championship|Championship]] in the fifth round draw, which took place on 30 October 2010. Matches were played in the week commencing 29 November 2010.<ref name="key_dates"/>

== Prize money ==
The prize money was awarded by the Football League. The winners of the League Cup won £100,000 and the runners-up won £50,000. The losing semi-finalists each took home £25,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.carling.com/contactus/footballQ.html |title=Football Queries |publisher=Carling.com |access-date=24 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120506043151/http://www.carling.com/contactus/footballQ.html |archive-date=6 May 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
